findings.detail: CONFIRMED FROM A REAL BUILD, NOT FROM THE REPORT. The reason asserted a universal about itself -- 'THIS LINE SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHETHER A LIFT IS EARNED and must not be read as saying so' -- in the same sentence run as its own per-arm clauses, every one of which says whether a lift is earned. On my 25,344-cell sweep the disclaimer printed on 19,574 cells and 19,574 of those (100%) also carried an earning assertion; 'NO LIFT IS EVER EARNED' appears in the same reason on the majority of them. THE FIX IS ONE CLAUSE AND WEAKENS NOTHING: the VERDICT is not a claim about earning, the LINE is full of them, so the sentence now reads 'THE VERDICT ABOVE IS NOT A CLAIM THAT NO LIFT IS EARNED and must not be read as one -- the clauses above say, per arm, which case it is in: ...'. The trailing '-- the clauses above say which case each arm is in' was removed as it is now the head of the sentence. AFTER: my classifier finds 0 self-contradicting reasons in 25,344 cells and 0 in the 430-cell frozen-surface sweep. THE CLASSIFIER IS SCOPE-AWARE ON PURPOSE, because a naive one produces false positives here: '(expert) NO LIFT IS EVER EARNED' beside '(vocabulary) lifts ARE earned here' is NOT a contradiction, the clauses are arm-scoped. It splits each reason into the gate's own voice and the per-arm clauses and applies five rules: (A) a gate-level universal about earning beside any earning assertion; (B) 'no lift reached the hard ceiling' beside 'SAID NO LIFT COULD BE HELD AT A CEILING HERE AND THE LEDGER DISAGREES'; (C) a value string whose clamped exceeds its lifts; (D) 'applied IN FULL' beside 'were CLAMPED'. Rule A fires 19,574 times before the fix and 0 after.

findings.symbol: src/capacity/api.py::_clamp_gate (the `falsified` clause on the armed-did-not-fire arm)
findings.detail: CONFIRMED AND FIXED, AND THE FIX IS FINER THAN THE ONE PROPOSED. `falsified` was computed once from `dead_facts` alone and appended to BOTH the FIRED and the lifts-only returns. On FIRED it is true; on lifts-only, clamped == 0 is exactly what the startup analysis predicted, so the ledger AGREES and the printed sentence said it disagrees. i_cap proposed keying the clause on `clamped` and, on the lifts-only arm, always saying the grounds are falsified. THAT IS NOT ALWAYS TRUE EITHER, and this is where the closed set earned its second job: five of the six grounds mean no lift is ever TAKEN on that arm (three because none is earned, plus at_ceiling and refused_unmasked because every earned one is refused before it is applied), but `inert` means a lift IS taken and moves nothing -- so on an inert ground, lifts > 0 with 0 clamped is what the analysis PREDICTS, not a contradiction of it. The arm now has three texts: clamped > 0 falsifies this gate's own reading; clamped == 0 with every ground in _CLAMP_KINDS_NO_LIFT_TAKEN falsifies the GROUNDS and says out loud that this gate's own reading stands; clamped == 0 with an `inert` ground prints agreement. NOT REACHABLE THROUGH A BUILD (dead_facts is passed only when neither arm has room, and there lifts = clamped = 0), which is why the 430-cell frozen-surface sweep exists.

findings.detail: IT WAS DOCUMENTATION AND IT IS NOW LOAD-BEARING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, PLUS A SECOND JOB. The tuple appeared only inside the fall-through ValueError's message, so it decided nothing: a kind with a branch and no tuple entry ran, and a tuple entry with no branch advertised itself as supported while raising. _clamp_blocked_clause now tests `kind not in _CLAMP_BLOCKED_KINDS` BEFORE dispatching -- so the tuple is the authority on what is accepted -- and the fall-through now reports the OTHER failure in its own words ('is declared in capacity/api.py::_CLAMP_BLOCKED_KINDS and no clause is written for it here'). AND IT IS NOW A PARTITION rather than a flat tuple: _CLAMP_KINDS_NO_LIFT_TAKEN + _CLAMP_KINDS_LIFT_TAKEN, whose concatenation IS the closed set, so the two halves cannot drift out of it. _clamp_gate reads the split for the finding above. unfinished.title: FOR THE OWNER -- Q-CAP-1, ITEM 4 written as a question: cap.clamp's UNREACHABLE population is an EXTENSION of D16, not a reading of it
unfinished.reason: It is a ruling and not a repair. The implementation is defensible and I did not change it -- the reachability predicate `expert_room or vocab_room` is untouched and my control shows zero verdict moves -- but an implementation that widens a ruling's population by about a factor of two, on grounds the ruling explicitly set aside, is making a decision. No check can catch it: nothing compares a Gate's verdict to .rework/DECISIONS.md.
unfinished.detail:
WHAT THE EXTENSION COVERS, MEASURED. .rework/DECISIONS.md D16's state table has exactly ONE UNREACHABLE row, on ONE ground: 'no lift can ever be earned | CAP_TARGETS excludes the arm | UNREACHABLE, per D15'. capacity/api.py::_clamp_gate reports UNREACHABLE on all SIX grounds in _CLAMP_BLOCKED_KINDS. On my 25,344-cell sweep, 19,574 cells are UNREACHABLE and carry 39,148 per-arm grounds (two per cell): unarmed 22,247, at_ceiling 9,243, refused_unmasked 2,732, nonpositive 2,395, never_pins 1,372, inert 1,159 (22,247+9,243+2,732+2,395+1,372+1,159 = 39,148 = 19,574 x 2). So 22,247 are D16's own row; 2,395 + 1,372 = 3,767 reach the STATE that row names by a cause the ruling does not mention; and 13,134 (9,243 + 2,732 + 1,159) do not reach that state at all, because there lifts ARE earned and are then refused by name or applied to no effect. D16's next paragraph names two of those three -- dead_rows_unmasked and lift_to returning the cap -- as cases that 'must not be mistaken for a clamp', and stops there: it does not say what verdict they carry.
WHY IT MIGHT WELL BE RIGHT. D16's verdict transfers on its own logic (where no lift is earned, none can be clamped), but this gate's subject is the CLAMP, not the lift. A clamp needs an APPLIED lift that overshoots a hard ceiling, and on all six grounds no such lift can exist, so the question is INAPPLICABLE rather than merely unmet -- which is what UNREACHABLE means under D15. Reporting '0 clamped of 0 lifts' on those 13,134 arm-grounds instead would read as a clamp that was live and never had to hold anything, i.e. the inert-versus-absent confusion the package exists to refuse.
WHAT THE OWNER HAS TO DECIDE. (a) CONFIRM: UNREACHABLE wherever no lift can be HELD AT A HARD CEILING, whatever the ground, and D16's table gains a row saying so. (b) SPLIT: UNREACHABLE only where no lift can be EARNED (26,014 of the 39,148 arm-grounds) and armed-but-0 where lifts are earned and lost (13,134). The document's recommendation is (a).
WHAT I CHANGED, WHICH IS THE FLAGGING AND NOT THE VERDICT: capacity/api.py::_clamp_gate's docstring made the argument as though it settled the matter; it now states the argument and then says 'It is NOT a ruling ... docs/04_CONTRACT.md carries it to the owner as Q-CAP-1'. The question is written out in full in docs/04_CONTRACT.md section 5 as '### Q-CAP-1 — `cap.clamp` reports UNREACHABLE on six grounds and `D16` ruled on one of them — **OPEN 2026-09-05: AN EXTENSION OF THE RULING, FLAGGED RATHER THAN TAKEN AS READ**'.

unfinished.detail: WHAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ALL SIX ROUNDS, and it is not expensive: the classifier I wrote for this task is 60 lines and needs no new machinery. It splits a rendered reason into the gate's own voice and its per-arm clauses (the '(expert)' / '(vocabulary)' markers), then applies a small table of (claim, contradictor) pairs at the right SCOPE -- a gate-level universal about earning against any earning assertion anywhere in the line; 'no lift reached the hard ceiling' against 'THE LEDGER DISAGREES' about that same claim; a value string whose clamped exceeds its lifts; 'applied IN FULL' beside 'were CLAMPED'. SCOPE IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: a naive pair-matcher fires on '(expert) NO LIFT IS EVER EARNED' beside '(vocabulary) lifts ARE earned here', which is two arms and not a contradiction, and a check that cries wolf there will be narrowed rather than obeyed. It has to run over RENDERED reasons from real builds, not over source text, because the contradiction is assembled at runtime from a helper's return value -- which is the same reason K15 abstains twice today ('the trace left the function'). My driver is at scratchpad/jd/sweep.py (contradictions() and split_scopes()) and is outside the repository; whoever owns tests/test_contract.py is welcome to it.
